text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Disy and Diko partnership in the government remains intact.
- Only 0.8 percent of the workforce in the private sector are women managers, survey shows.
- Partners scramble to save the government coalition. Diko gives Disy one last chance to save the ailing partnership.
- Shares continue record tumble on Cyprus exchange as fears grow of long-term damage to the economy.
- Seven in 10 Cypriots want cost of living allowances preserved.
- Diko party president Spyros Kyprianou gives partners Disy one last chance to improve relations.
- Policemen take backhanders from foreign students who want a residence permit, says a member of parliament.
- Senior Disy party members exercise self-criticism over party decisions in an attempt to bring unity back to the party.
- The Dutch presidency of the EU and the United States will coordinate their efforts to bring about a solution to the Cyprus problem.
